story.title: ANC Faces Significant Defeat in South Africa's Local Elections
story.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive around 30% of the vote in South Africa's recent local elections, marking its lowest electoral performance to date. With over 80% of ballots counted, the party's share is significantly lower than its results in previous elections, indicating a continued decline for the once-dominant political force. The election results are expected to lead to coalition negotiations in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed for the ANC?
explore_lenses.title: From local-government leader to fragmented councils
explore_lenses.summary: With 99% of ballots counted, reporting put the ANC at about 30% of valid votes—its weakest local-election result—while the DA led in several major Gauteng metros previously led by the ANC. The result does not by itself determine who governs: many councils lack an outright majority.

claims.text: At roughly 99% counted, the ANC had about 30% of the national vote, its worst result in a local-government election.

The DA was on course to become the largest party in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, according to AP and preliminary results reporting; that changes the bargaining position in the country’s largest economic metro area.
The ANC acknowledged that its support had fallen and that it had lost councils it had long governed, while saying the final figures rested with the Electoral Commission.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in hung metros?
explore_lenses.title: Councils must choose their leadership within 14 days
explore_lenses.summary: Coalition talks are political negotiations, not an automatic consequence of finishing first. Once councillors are declared elected, municipal councils must convene and elect office-bearers, including speakers and mayors where applicable.

claims.text: The Electoral Commission said on November 7 that it was determining objections, had ordered recounts in five wards, and that provisional seat assignments could change after objections are decided.
Under section 29(2) of the Municipal Structures Act, the municipal manager—or a provincial designee if necessary—must convene a newly elected council within 14 days after it is declared elected.
At those first meetings, councillors elect the speaker and, where applicable, the mayor or executive mayor and deputy positions; coalition agreements can determine which bloc can win those votes.

The DA’s federal executive said it would negotiate with parties that support its stated priorities of accountable government, anti-corruption measures, service delivery, rule of law and non-racialism.

explore_lenses.label: How do the ANC and DA explain the result?
explore_lenses.title: Both frame the vote around governance and service delivery
explore_lenses.summary: The ANC treated the result as a rebuke over its local-government record and promised internal renewal. The DA characterized its gains as a mandate for stable, accountable municipal coalitions; these are party interpretations rather than independently established causal findings.

claims.text: The ANC said it had fallen short on local services, citing water access, refuse collection, road maintenance, billing problems and misuse of public money in some places.
The ANC said it would approach coalition discussions in good faith, with service continuity and constitutionally grounded priorities, while its national executive considered the party’s position.
The DA said its coalition goal was stable, effective municipal government focused on accountability and service delivery, and that negotiations would be coordinated by its federal executive.

Forecast: the Bureau for Economic Research said the leading party in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni was expected to fall short of an outright majority, making coalition negotiations unavoidable if that projection held.

story_report.summary: South Africa’s African National Congress was headed for about 30% of the national vote with roughly 99% counted in local-government elections, its worst result in such a contest. The result left the party acknowledging lost support and councils it had long governed. In Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, the Democratic Alliance was on course to lead the vote, while no leading party was expected to secure an outright majority, setting up negotiations over control of key municipal governments.

sections.heading: Metro Results Shift Bargaining Power
sections.body: Preliminary results put the DA on course to become the largest party in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, altering its bargaining position in the country’s largest economic metro area. The Bureau for Economic Research forecast that the leading party in each of those metros would fall short of a majority, making coalition talks necessary if the projection holds. The ANC attributed part of its loss to shortcomings in local services, including water access, refuse collection, road maintenance, billing and misuse of public money in some areas.

sections.heading: Council Votes Will Determine Control
sections.body: The Electoral Commission said it was determining objections and had ordered recounts in five wards; provisional seat allocations could change once those cases are decided. After a council is declared elected, the municipal manager, or a provincial designee where necessary, must convene its first meeting within 14 days. Councillors then elect speakers and, where applicable, mayors, executive mayors and deputies, making coalition agreements central to who can win those posts.

sections.heading: Parties Set Conditions for Talks
sections.body: The ANC said it would enter coalition discussions in good faith, prioritising continuity of services and constitutionally grounded principles while its national executive considered the party’s position. The DA said negotiations would be coordinated by its federal executive and limited to parties backing accountable government, anti-corruption measures, service delivery, the rule of law and non-racialism. These are party positions rather than settled governing arrangements.

unresolved.text: The Electoral Commission’s final declaration, including decisions on objections and recounts, will determine the official municipal allocations.
No coalition partner, mayoral candidate or governing agreement is assured until agreements are concluded and newly elected councils vote.

related_stories.title: Eisenkot Receives Mandate to Form Government Amid Crisis Concerns in Israel
related_stories.summary: Eisenkot, a political newcomer, has been formally tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming a new government in Israel. He has 28 days to achieve this despite his bloc not holding a clear majority. Eisenkot emphasized the need for trustworthy leadership that represents all segments of society, amid warnings of a potential crisis under the current government led by Netanyahu.

related_stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot Assigned to Form New Israeli Government After Elections
related_stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government following the inconclusive results of the October 28 elections. Eisenkot, who leads an anti-Netanyahu alliance, has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition capable of securing a parliamentary majority. The process is expected to be challenging, with potential alliances being politically sensitive.

related_stories.title: Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff Following Midterm Defeat
related_stories.summary: Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Miller, known for his hardline stance on immigration and as a key architect of Trump's mass deportation policies, is expected to reinforce Trump's agenda following a disappointing midterm election. His appointment may lead to increased tensions with Congress as the administration prepares for upcoming challenges.
